questions.prompt: For style references in its Recipes, what do the Runway docs recommend?

options.text: A single image, as large and sharp as you can get
options.explanation: The Runway docs say a few complementary images define a style more reliably than one.

options.text: A few images with a shared palette, light and mood
options.explanation: Right. The Runway docs call it a small, cohesive set.

options.text: As many images as the model will accept per request
options.explanation: Runway does not recommend filling the limit. It recommends a small, cohesive set.

questions.prompt: In Runway's guide for its Recipes, what should you do with references that have conflicting looks?

options.text: Put them in one request so the model can blend them
options.explanation: The Runway docs say not to mix conflicting aesthetics in a single request.

options.text: Add more images of each look, so the model averages them
options.explanation: The Runway docs say not to mix conflicting aesthetics in a single request. More images add more conflict.

options.text: Generate the looks separately, then curate the results
options.explanation: Right. Runway's wording is "generate separately and curate".

questions.prompt: Every result shows the wooden shelf from your three object photos. What is the likely cause?

options.text: All three photos share one shelf, so the model treats it as part of the object
options.explanation: Right. This is our reading of Anthropic's advice that examples should be diverse. Vary what you do not want copied.

options.text: Three photos are too few for any model to read, so it has to guess the rest
options.explanation: Three is a normal size. The problem is what the three have in common.
